text.p: Eurotunnel SA said on Thursday it had asked the British and French governments to extend its operating concession to 999 years from 65 years at present.

Co-chairman Patrick Ponsolle told a news conference Eurotunnel believed it should be given the same operating concession as was granted to London and Continental Railways last year for operating the new British fast rail link between London and the Channel Tunnel.
"Our official requirement is for Eurotunnel to enjoy the same length of concession that is going to be enjoyed by LNCR," Ponsolle said.
"We see no reason why we should not enjoy the same length of concession," he said.
Ponsolle said extending the concession was essential to securing banks' and shareholders' approval for the debt restructuring plan.
He said he hoped a deal with the governments could be reached within the next few weeks in time for publication of the debt restructuring prospectus in the second half of May.
